senses.sense_definition: The collection of traditional stories and beliefs of a specific culture, often involving gods, heroes, and the origins of the world.

examples.text: The <w>mythology</w> of ancient Greece is filled with powerful gods and legendary heroes.
Students often study Norse <w>mythology</w> to understand the cultural roots of Scandinavian people.

senses.sense_definition: The academic study and systematic collection of myths.

examples.text: The professor dedicated her career to the <w>mythology</w> of indigenous tribes in the Americas.
Advanced <w>mythology</w> requires a deep understanding of historical and anthropological contexts.

senses.sense_definition: A set of widely held but false beliefs or misconceptions about a person, group, or subject.

examples.text: The <w>mythology</w> surrounding the company's success ignores the many failures they faced early on.
We must challenge the <w>mythology</w> that suggests success is only possible through luck.

senses.sense_definition: A body of stories or beliefs that develop around a specific event, person, or institution.

examples.text: A complex <w>mythology</w> has grown around the life of the famous revolutionary leader.
The <w>mythology</w> of the war often obscures the harsh realities faced by the soldiers.

senses.sense_definition: The internal lore, history, and fictional background of a creative work or universe.

examples.text: Fans of the series enjoy discussing the intricate <w>mythology</w> of the fictional world.
The show's <w>mythology</w> became too complicated for new viewers to follow easily.
